issues: No sign of getting around the measurement. The candidate reads no files, pastes in no answers and never touches test labels. brics_counts builds features from test_smiles only, the same way the incumbent already does for fingerprints and descriptors.

No bug that would make the result meaningless. The BRICS fragment hash (character codes weighted by position, mod 1024) is deterministic, so features are the same on every run. The min-max kernel on non-negative counts is a valid kernel, and the denominator is clamped at 1e-9. BRICSDecompose always returns at least one fragment, so no molecule gets an all-zero row and the kernel diagonal stays 1.
Minor robustness note: if Chem.MolFromSmiles returns None, BRICSDecompose will crash. The incumbent's featurizers presumably parse the same SMILES, so this adds no new risk.

Cost looks fine. The minmax loop does about n_test+n_train row passes over arrays of about 776x1024, which is cheap. BRICS decomposition adds some per-fit time but should stay far below the 10-minute limit.
